# `crossspectrum`

the sensor cross-spectral density per band (Welch), on a kernel's channels or the good imaging channels.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run crossspectrum --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run crossspectrum --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run crossspectrum --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all [--channels-of KERNEL] --bands '[{"name": "alpha", "lo": 8, "hi": 12}]' [--resolve bins]
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recording` | field recording, each true, where {"name": "$recording"} | yes |
| `channels_of` | operator any, from recording.manifold.0, where {"name": "$channels_of"}, required false | no |
| `bad` | selection spans, manifold recording.time, where {"name": "{recording}_bad_segments"}, required false | no |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recording` | `--recording` | `none` | - |  | the recording's name, or none: every recording of the subject, one run each |
| `channels_of` | `--channels-of` | none | - |  | an operator (a kernel) whose channels are the ones covered, in order; null: the good channels of channel_types |
| `channel_types` | `--channel-types` | `["MEG", "MEG MAG", "MEG GRAD", "EEG", "SEEG", "ECOG"]` | - |  | the channel types covered when channels_of is null (good channels only) |
| `name` | `--name` | `{recording}_crossspectrum` | - |  | the stored statistic's name; beside it <name>_channels, <name>_segments, and with resolve bins <name>_bins |
| `bands` | `--bands` | `required` | Hz |  | the bands, the caller's choice (no default): a list of {name, lo, hi}, e.g. --bands '[{"name": "alpha", "lo": 8, "hi": 12}]'; a band holds the bins from lo to hi inclusive |
| `resolve` | `--resolve` | `band` | - | band, bins | band = each band one member (its bins averaged) \| bins = also every bin of each band |
| `segment_seconds` | `--segment-seconds` | `4.0` | s |  | the segment's length in seconds (under segment_rule tile it snaps to the nearest 2^k samples) |
| `segment_samples` | `--segment-samples` | none | samples |  | the segment's length in samples (wins over segment_seconds); null: from segment_seconds |
| `segment_rule` | `--segment-rule` | `tile` | - | tile, round, even | how the segment's length becomes samples: tile \| round \| even |
| `overlap` | `--overlap` | `0.5` | fraction |  | the fraction of a segment shared with the next, in [0, 1) |
| `window` | `--window` | `hamming` | - | hann, hamming, blackman, rectangular | the taper of each segment |
| `periodic` | `--periodic` | false | - |  | the DFT-even form of the window rather than the symmetric one |
| `detrend` | `--detrend` | `constant` | - | none, constant, linear | what is removed from each segment before windowing |
| `scaling` | `--scaling` | `density` | - | density, spectrum, chain | density = power per Hz \| spectrum = power \| chain = per sample, per bin |
| `bad_segments` | `--bad-segments` | `exclude` | - | exclude, ignore | exclude = a segment touching one of the recording's bad segments is left out \| ignore = every segment is kept |

## Presets

`--set <preset>` sets the parameters below at once; a parameter given by name wins over the preset.

| preset | sets |
|---|---|
| `tiles` | segment_rule=tile |
| `brainstorm` | segment_rule=round, window=hamming, periodic=false, detrend=constant, scaling=density |
| `scipy` | segment_rule=round, window=hann, periodic=true, detrend=constant, scaling=density |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chunks over `recording` | [`signal.xpsd`](../nodes.md) | x=recording, channels_of=channels_of, exclude=bad | bands=$bands, channel_types=$channel_types, resolve=$resolve, segment_seconds=$segment_seconds, segment_samples=$segment_samples, segment_rule=$segment_rule, overlap=$overlap, window=$window, periodic=$periodic, detrend=$detrend, scaling=$scaling, bad_segments=$bad_segments | channels, spectrum, bins |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `channels` | kind selection, type indices, name $name_channels, on recording.manifold.0 |
| `spectrum` | kind statistic, name $name, of recording, axes [{"name": "band"}, {"name": "channel", "selection": "channels"}, {"name": "channel", "selection": "channels"}], partition {"tiling": "$name_segments", "on": "recording.time"} |
| `bins` | kind statistic, optional true, name $name_bins, of recording, axes [{"name": "frequency"}, {"name": "channel", "selection": "channels"}, {"name": "channel", "selection": "channels"}], partition {"tiling": "$name_segments", "on": "recording.time"} |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE SENSOR CROSS-SPECTRUM PER BAND (a statistic): C[a, b] = <X_a conj(X_b)> over the Welch segments (streamed chunk by chunk, the recording's bad segments left out), the mean over
each band's bins, on the channels of an operator (channels_of: a kernel, so a source estimate K C K^T reads it) or the good channels of the imaging types. A sensor quantity: what a
source estimate makes of it is the kernel's. With resolve bins, also every bin of each band (the band's value is the mean of them).
Stored: the statistic `<name>` (band x channel x channel, complex; a band k is read by its old name `<name>_<band>`), its channels `<name>_channels`, its segment partition
`<name>_segments`, and with resolve bins `<name>_bins` (frequency x channel x channel).

  nxr-neuro run crossspectrum --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all [--channels-of KERNEL] --bands '[{"name": "alpha", "lo": 8, "hi": 12}]' [--resolve bins]
The bands are required: no band set is assumed (a refused run names how to pass them).
```
